title_guess: Inflation, disinflation, deflation and reflation on the price-index curve

segments.teaches: prices are tracked at two points of the supply chain: wholesale basket (WPI) and household consumption basket (CPI)

elements.what: producer factory -> wholesaler warehouse -> retailer shop -> consumer, blue captions
cart piled with boxes over the wholesaler-to-retailer arrow (wholesale basket)
shopping trolley over the retailer-to-consumer arrow (household basket)
blue box under the first basket and yellow box under the second, each describing what the basket holds
under each box: 'price movement measured by' -> index name (WPI / CPI)

segments.notes: Recap of earlier inflation-measurement lessons; colour of each box (blue/yellow) stays tied to its index.

segments.teaches: on a price-index-over-time curve: rising stretch = inflation; rising but flattening = disinflation (slower inflation); falling = deflation

elements.what: small stack: price index up-arrow over average price level over WPI / CPI, which then moves to the top-left as the graph title

year on x-axis, price index on a right-side y-axis; dotted line chart with rising parts highlighted yellow and labelled inflation along the slope, flat top highlighted green (disinflation), falling part highlighted pink (deflation)
tilted white card with the inflation definition
green-text box above the flat top: inflation rate declining
faded tilted pink card with the deflation definition below the dip

segments.notes: Labels are written along the curve's slope. Each phase is coloured by laying a translucent marker stroke over that part of the line.

segments.teaches: the same phases spotted on India's real consumer price index from 2018 to 2022

elements.what: real CPI line chart (2018-2022) pasted in with its data-source caption
orange marker strokes over the rising stretches, each labelled inflation along the slope
green stroke over a flat stretch labelled disinflation, with a down-arrow
pink strokes over the dips, joined by arrows to one deflation label
round stickers with ticks: yellow on inflation, green on disinflation, purple on deflation

segments.notes: Moves from an idealised curve to real data. The chart is a third-party screenshot; BIE should plot its own data. Colour code (yellow/green/purple) carries over from the previous segment.

segments.teaches: why deflation is a problem: falling prices make people delay buying, demand falls, profits fall, bad loans and unemployment rise

elements.what: pink card: deflation title, purple tick sticker, line down to 'prices falling'
big black ? on the card's corner (so what is wrong with that?)
prices falling -> demand decreases -> profits decrease, in plain capital words
white speech box over demand decreases: buyers wait for lower prices
profits decrease splits by elbow arrows into increased NPAs and increased unemployment

segments.notes: When the chart clears, only the deflation label and its tick sticker stay on the blank canvas; the card is then built around them, so one object carries over between compositions.

segments.teaches: the government responds by raising the price level (reflation): more public spending, tax cuts and interest-rate cuts

elements.what: dark full-width band sliding up from the bottom with one white sentence on the policy response

segments.notes: Lower-third caption band used as the conclusion; the diagram above stays visible. The word reflation is not written on screen in the sampled frames.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels with app promo
